** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Text readers can return parsed values under Axios 0.27.x.** The declared `axios >=0.27` range includes 0.27.x. In 0.27.x, `forcedJSONParsing` defaults to `true`. The response transform parses string bodies even when `responseType` is `"text"`. A body that is entirely valid JSON, such as `"123"`, then returns as a number, not a string. The `getTextMessage`, `getRawMessage`, `getMessageHtmlSource`, `getHtmlMessage`, and `getMessageAsEml` methods can all return these values. The repository lockfile resolves Axios 1.20.0, which skips forced parsing when `responseType` is set. The defect appears only when a consumer resolves Axios 0.27.x. Override the response transform for these readers with an identity transform. Alternatively, disable forced JSON parsing for each request. Add coverage that runs against the oldest supported Axios version in the declared range.

After applying the fix, consider running `coderabbit review --agent` for local review. Visit https://docs.coderabbit.ai/cli?utm_source=ghpr ```

** Minor** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win** **Skip the JSON decode for responses that Axios already parsed.** For requests without `responseType: "text"`, Axios decodes the response body before this handler runs. A JSON string body is therefore decoded once by Axios. `buildErrorMessage` then parses it again. For a body such as `"{\"errors\":{\"name\":\"invalid\"}}"`, the second parse yields an object whose `errors.name` is a string. `errors.name.join(", ")` at line 171 then throws `TypeError`, and the `MailtrapError` is never constructed. Gate the parse on the request's response type. The parse is needed only when Axios leaves the body as raw text, which is the `responseType: "text"` case that the message readers use.
Suggested fix

```diff if ( + error.config?.responseType === "text" && typeof data === "string" && /application\/(?:[\w.+-]+\+)?json\b/i.test(String(contentType)) ) { ```

Five message retrieval methods now request text responses from Axios. Error handling attempts to parse matching JSON response bodies before extracting an error message. **Changes: Message Response Handling** |Layer / File(s)|Summary| |:---|:---| |**Text response retrieval**

`src/lib/axios-logger.ts`, `src/__tests__/lib/api/resources/Messages.test.ts`|`buildErrorMessage` attempts to parse string response bodies when the response content type matches JSON. If parsing fails, it keeps the original text. A test checks that a JSON 404 response produces the message `"Not found"`.| **Estimated code review effort:** 2 (Simple) | ~10 minutes **Change:** Bug fix **Suggested reviewers:** `narekhovhannisyan`
Merge Risk: Low · up to bc9d0

The change makes the five message-body readers return text and decodes JSON error messages. Under the default install (Axios 1.x) this works as intended. Consumers pinned to Axios 0.27.x may still receive parsed values from the text readers. A double-encoded JSON error body can also surface a TypeError instead of a MailtrapError. These are narrow edge cases, so the PR is mergeable with minor follow-up.
